analysis.investment_thesis: Gravita is a competent recycler benefiting from India's Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations which create some structural demand for its lead and aluminium recycling. However, at 31.7x P/E with thin 12% operating margins, the price already reflects the good news, and the inherently commodity-linked business lacks the durable pricing power I require.
key_strengths: Impressive 9-year revenue CAGR of 27.6% and net profit CAGR of 58.4%, demonstrating consistent execution and scale
Conservative balance sheet with D/E of only 0.20 and borrowings declining to INR 445 Cr in 2025 despite heavy expansion
EPR compliance services and turnkey recycling solutions create some stickiness with industrial customers beyond pure commodity trading
key_risks: Operating margins are thin at 11.96% and highly exposed to lead/aluminium scrap price volatility — a commodity business without pricing power
Free cash flow is erratic (negative in 2022 and 2024, only 175 Cr positive in 2025) despite strong reported profits, signaling working capital intensity
Massive investing outflow of INR 864 Cr in 2025 funded largely by equity raise (+640 Cr financing CF) — growth is capital-hungry and dilutive
red_flags: Other Income of INR 111 Cr in 2025 is nearly 35% of operating income — unusually high and inflates reported profitability
Total equity nearly tripled in one year (837→2,260 Cr) suggesting a large QIP/equity raise that dilutes existing holders
Capital-intensive business with continuous capex (INR 73–108 Cr/year) generating poor incremental returns on invested capital
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Gravita runs a solid recycling operation with genuine tailwinds from India's EPR regulations, but it is fundamentally a commodity-processing business. Lead and aluminium scrap prices dictate margins far more than any competitive advantage, which shows up in the volatile free cash flow — negative in two of the last four years despite strong net profit growth. The recycling sector requires constant working capital and capital expenditure to maintain throughput, limiting the owner earnings I care about.

At a 31.7x P/E (forward 23x), the market is pricing in sustained high growth that depends on commodity cycle cooperation and continued regulatory tailwinds. The dramatic equity dilution in 2025 to fund expansion is a yellow flag — truly wonderful businesses fund growth internally. I'd want this at 15–18x earnings before getting interested.
